subject: Clarifying log/backups retention and deletion SLA — follow-up from demo
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@medlark.com>, Tom Evans <tom.evans@medlark.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: log/backup retention and deletion SLA (post-demo)

Hi Aisha / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the time and the frank discussion about compliance needs. Quick recap and our asks so we can get your vendor review moving: 

Summary from our side:
- Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified (we can share the report).
- We support GDPR and HIPAA scopes depending on deployment (hosted + Private).
- Logs and backups are configurable by plan; there are defaults we typically document.

A few questions you raised that I want to make sure we address formally for your vendor team: 
1) What is Redwood's retention window for application logs, security/analysis logs, and backups (including full snapshots vs incremental copies)?
2) When a customer requests deletion of account data, what is the SLA for primary deletion and for deletion/purge of backups or snapshot copies?
3) Are backups encrypted at-rest with KMS-managed keys, and do you offer customer-managed KMS for Private/Dedicated?
4) Can you provide evidence of deletion (audit log entry, job id) we can attach to our vendor intake?

Next steps I propose:
- If you can complete the short vendor questionnaire attached to your reply, we’ll map answers and share Redwood's SOC2 and deletion process docs.
- Ben (cc'd) will provide the canonical retention numbers and deletion SLA in a follow-up.
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call with Product Security to walk through the deletion lifecycle and backup architecture.

Thanks — I’ll wait for your questionnaire and any additional questions.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the recap. Good alignment overall. A few clarifications from our InfoSec perspective so we can complete the vendor evaluation: 

High-level: MediLark needs vendors to demonstrate SOC2 Type II (or equivalent), encryption for backups, documented deletion processes, and proof of deletion events. We run a standard vendor questionnaire to capture those items.

Specifics we need answered: 
- Retention windows for: 
  * application logs (user-level, PII-containing entries)
  * security logs (authN/authZ, alerting, IDS)
  * periodic full snapshots and incremental backups (how many copies, where stored, retention per copy)
- Deletion SLA: within how many days do you remove primary data upon request, and what is the timeline to fully purge backups/snapshots?
- If backups are geo-replicated, are those replicas purged automatically or do they require separate retention operations?
- Encryption/key management: are backups encrypted with KMS keys; do you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for Private deployments?
- Do you provide an audit artifact (job id / timestamped log) that shows deletion completion?

I’ve attached our vendor questionnaire — please have your security or engineering team complete pages 2–4, and return. We’d like written answers for the three bullet items above to include in our procurement packet.

Also, one additional ask: for FedRAMP/HIPAA scoping, can you confirm which Redwood components (control plane, inference nodes, backups) would be in-scope for an on-prem Private deployment versus your hosted offering?

We’re aiming to close the vendor assessment this month, so a response by EOD Wednesday (6/23) would be perfect.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
CISO, MediLark Health
aisha.khan@medlark.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: log/backup retention and deletion SLA (post-demo)

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. I’m Ben (Head of Security Operations) — below are the canonical answers and attachments. I’ll also add a few operational notes at the bottom.

Retention (defaults for Redwood hosted API):
- Application logs (request/response metadata, non-PII traces): 30 days live. Aggregated/ingestion logs used for security and billing: 13 months (configurable for Enterprise).
- Security logs (authN/authZ, audit events): 13 months by default; we retain detailed audit trails for 13 months and summarized indices for longer.
- Backups / snapshots: full backups (snapshots) retained for 90 days by default; incremental backups kept in object storage for tiered retention windows — default 90 days, can be extended to 365+ under a Dedicated/Private contract.

Deletion SLA and process:
- Primary customer data deletion request: Redwood deletes primary data within 30 days of a validated request (we mark the account for deletion, remove live keys, and scrub primary stores).
- Backups / snapshot purge: by default backups are scheduled for purge within 90 days of deletion; backups are immutable copies and require background retention cycles to compact and remove copies. Expedited purge options are available by contract (expedited purge target: 14 days) with a compliance addendum.
- Geo-replicated copies are subject to the same retention/ purge policy; purge runs in each replica region but may finish at slightly different times (we provide a purge job id and timestamps).

Encryption & Key Management:
- All backups and snapshot objects are encrypted at rest using AES-256. For hosted customers we manage the KMS keys; for Dedicated/Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and HSM integrations.

Audit evidence:
- We provide an audit artifact for deletion events: job id, initiating principal, and timestamps. Those records are available in the audit logs and can be exported as CSV or included in a compliance package.

In-scope components by deployment model:
- Hosted (Redwood-managed): control plane + inference nodes + backups are in Redwood's scope for SOC2.
- Private (customer-managed infrastructure): control plane can be run in a customer VPC; backups and key management can be put under customer-managed KMS — scope depends on deployment choices, we’ll include a recommended scoping doc.

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (internal SOC2 report stub). I’ve also pasted a short deletion timeline example below for your packet.

Example deletion timeline (for procurement packet):
- Day 0: Customer submits validated deletion request via support portal or signed request.
- Day 0–1: Account flagged, primary keys rotated and credentials revoked.
- Day 1–30: Primary data deleted from live stores; confirmation artifact generated (job id).
- Day 31–90: Background retention compaction runs remove backup snapshots; final purge job completes; audit artifact generated for backup purge.

If you want a shorter backup purge window (e.g., 45 days), we can include an expedited purge addendum and provide the associated operational runbook and SLA. Happy to jump on a quick call with our product-security engineer (Laura) to walk through the runbook.

Ben Carter
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
